title: Expanded Luna prompt study: selective gains, important regressions
conclusion: Readable task-specific instructions improve some evidence boundaries, but the complete revision set is not safe to deploy. Reject the sampling-plan revision; revise action execution and narrative-ending rules before deployment. Large lossless semantic normalization remains unresolved.
review_method: Assistant paired review, not blinded human assessment. Short actions, stories, extractions, summaries, names, scoring and validation questions were read. Long biographies, documents, memories and sampling spaces received targeted constraint/field/section review, not exhaustive line-by-line semantic certification. All complete inputs and outputs are preserved. Normalization uses exact occurrence-multiset checks plus category samples. Automatic checks never imply semantic success.
limitations: The 8,839-observation corpus is the source pool, not the number of cases tested. This experiment used 52 distinct source observations and 106 calls.
One fresh baseline and one fresh revision per primary source, with additional development-only normalization variants; not a repeated-trial reliability estimate.
The 24 validation inputs were scenario-reserved from current tuning, not historically unseen, persona-disjoint or prompt-template-disjoint.
Only six families have reserved validation examples. Vision, extraction, scoring, normalization, sampling, document enrichment and other uncovered families have development-only evidence.
Exact cached histories are fixed. No full simulation rollout, rerun notebook comparison, population calibration or one-call persona diversity repair is established.
Validation instructions were frozen before selected reserved contents were accessed. No validation failures were tuned away.
All calls completed, but completion and schema validity are not quality passes.
Costs use saved list-price rates and response usage, not invoices. Missing cache-write counts produce explicit bounds, not assumed zero writes.

families.finding: Development turns remain relevant and usually shorter; the political-debate revision reduces repetition. In the reserved translation case, however, the baseline asks the attendant where to stand, while the revision gives Zog a suggested phrase and then waits for a reply despite not asking the attendant.
families.decision: Do not deploy as-is. Evidence caution must not replace an available requested action with advice or a promise.

families.finding: Required top-level fields are present. Sampled ages, occupations and supplied contexts are coherent on both sides. Revised profiles record constraints more explicitly, but practical, conscientious, cautious professionals/caregivers still dominate. More biography or a different city is not evidence that the one-call diversity problem is solved.
families.decision: Keep experimental; no claim of diversity, population calibration or exhaustive biography fidelity.

families.finding: Both versions correctly extract Hector's option 2 and Marisol's B-E-D-C-A ranking from public TALK. Revised justifications remain public-source grounded, but these easy positive examples do not demonstrate improved handling of missing public answers.
families.decision: Compatible with earlier evidence-scope improvements; this new pair set alone does not establish a new fix.

families.finding: Revisions retain Diana's overcommitment/money worries, Joanne's impatience, Julian's over-researching, Rafael's self-promotion/family-time tension and Camila's limits of expertise instead of listing only virtues. Reserved profiles generally preserve more distinctive source-grounded tension. This is complementary-summary quality, not proof of better subsequent behavior.
families.decision: Promising candidate for a separate runtime integration and rollout check.

families.finding: Both versions often preserve unresolved evidence and dated-report boundaries. Revised samples more explicitly distinguish a reported claim about Zog from independently established origin, and planned web consultation from a recorded web-search result. Long financial details have not been exhaustively audited for every omission or numerical error.
families.decision: Retain as candidate, not an all-details-preserved certification.

families.finding: Both retain scores 9 and 8, explanations and disabled-check qualifications. The Reese input already labels B-first versus D-first-among-devices inconsistent, although B means no device. Repeating that upstream assessment is faithful synthesis, not independent confirmation that the assessment is correct.
families.decision: No established new quality gain; distinguish faithful synthesis from validity of upstream scoring.

families.finding: Both fresh baselines and both revisions exceed the actual fivefold character requirement. MultiLever baseline/revision: 5.78x/5.41x; Kestrel: 6.69x/9.35x. Source boundaries and useful document sections were sampled, not exhaustively audited. Extra length is not automatically better.
families.decision: Do not credit this experiment with repairing the historical short-document failure.

families.finding: The development consulting revision avoids invented completed findings. On reserved inputs all four revisions satisfy the 100-word limit versus one of four baselines. The normal-week revision does not invent an agent's personal incident. But the two requested endings remain weak/open: the heat alert is unresolved and the scheduling demo is left as a prompt rather than a verdict. Authorized fictional continuation is not automatically hallucination; the ending requirement takes precedence over generic open-endedness.
families.decision: Do not deploy unchanged. Make narrative authority and an explicit ending override clearer, without inventing agent achievements.

families.finding: Both catch Nadia's degree versus no-formal-education expectation and ask behavioral probes. Luisa's revision is shorter with fewer repeated luxury/status questions; prior answers already explicitly rejected those expectations, so that reduction is not automatically lost evidence.
families.decision: No measured assessment-accuracy gain; these are interview/question-generation comparisons.

families.verdict: Better evidence scope in one case
families.finding: Gabriela's baseline penalizes unspecified ranking/screen preferences, while the revision correctly distinguishes absence of a prescription from a contradiction and acknowledges the cost trade-off. Another source scores 9 in both. The improvement is the reasoning, not the higher number.
families.decision: Promising development-only clarification; retain the original scale and missing-evidence rules.

families.finding: Baseline/revision propose 85/74 dimensions; all checked weighted categorical totals equal one. This does not establish correct conditional populations, independence or joint demographic/behavioral calibration. Long source and output fields were reviewed selectively.
families.decision: Do not treat arithmetic or rich coverage as a quality pass.

families.finding: Both totals equal N=70, but the revision invents technology_and_screen_time and rewrites permitted values in three directives. The baseline uses only known dimensions and exact permitted values. The revision is also much longer. Exact total alone would have hidden this regression.
families.decision: Retain baseline behavior. Any future candidate must pass exact dimension/value/range checks before usefulness is assessed.

families.finding: Both return plausible name-only scalar values inside the required schema. Reserved exclusions include empty and nonempty lists; no observed exclusion collision. Eleanor Whitaker still recurs across independent requests, so per-list uniqueness is not population diversity.
families.decision: No established quality improvement or global diversity guarantee.

families.finding: Both generate concise plausible Colombian-context names without added biography: Adriana Lucia Echeverri versus Diana Carolina Beltran. One pair cannot establish improved cultural accuracy or reduced repetition.

families.verdict: Unresolved; reject all tested large-input variants
families.finding: 815-member baseline preserves zero exact original members; v1 retains only 84. V2 copies all 815 but collapses them into one generic category, losing useful clustering. V3 produces six themes but only 710 output occurrences and an overlength label. On the independent 225-member control, baseline returns 224 and v3 226 occurrences; neither multiset is exact. The one-member control passes on both sides and is trivial.
families.decision: Prompt prose alone did not reliably combine useful grouping with exact copying. An index-assignment contract with deterministic reconstruction is a plausible separate experiment, not implemented or validated here.

families.finding: Actual image is a green/yellow lizard humanoid with bow and quiver. Baseline executes surrounding scene instructions and asks Talia/Jordan how their characters respond. Revision describes the visible image instead, without running the scene.
families.decision: Strong localized development example; no held-out vision reliability estimate.
